examples.en: Only when you're healthy can you also enjoy your work.

22.summary: てこそ says 'only by doing X can you achieve or understand Y'.
22.details:
自分でやってみ**てこそ**、その難しさが分かる。
*(Only when you try it yourself do you understand how hard it is.)*
健康であっ**てこそ**、仕事も楽しめる。
*(Only when you're healthy can you also enjoy your work.)*

こそ (N3) emphasizes the て-clause as the essential condition. The second clause usually expresses a positive value (分かる, 意味がある, 本物だ). With nouns and adjectives use であってこそ.

22.title: 〜てならない
22.structure: Verb (て-form) / い-Adj (〜くて) / な-Adj (〜で) + ならない
22.explanation: A feeling arises naturally and is so strong the speaker can't stop it.

examples.jp: 試験の結果が気になってならない。
examples.en: I can't stop worrying about the exam results.

examples.jp: 故郷の両親のことが心配でならない。
examples.en: I'm terribly worried about my parents back home.

22.summary: てならない describes a feeling so strong it can't be held back — 'can't help feeling'.
22.details:
試験の結果が気になっ**てならない**。
*(I can't stop worrying about the exam results.)*
故郷の両親のことが心配**でならない**。
*(I'm terribly worried about my parents back home.)*

Used with feelings and perceptions that arise by themselves: 気になる, 心配だ, 残念だ, 思える, 感じられる. It is similar to てたまらない and てしょうがない (N3) but more formal; for physical sensations like pain or heat, てたまらない is the more natural choice.

23.title: 〜にかかわらず
23.structure: Noun + にかかわらず / Verb (Dictionary) + Verb (ない-form) + にかかわらず
23.explanation: Something applies equally whatever the condition is, usually with pairs of opposites or words for variation.

examples.jp: 天候にかかわらず、試合は行われます。
examples.en: The match will be held regardless of the weather.

examples.jp: 参加するしないにかかわらず、メールで返事をください。
examples.en: Whether you'll participate or not, please reply by email.

23.summary: にかかわらず means 'regardless of X' — the outcome doesn't depend on it.
23.details:
天候**にかかわらず**、試合は行われます。
*(The match will be held regardless of the weather.)*
参加するしない**にかかわらず**、メールで返事をください。
*(Whether you'll participate or not, please reply by email.)*

Takes nouns of variation (天候, 年齢, 性別, 経験) or opposites (する・しない, 好き嫌い). Don't confuse with にもかかわらず (Lesson 2), which means 'despite'. Written 関わらず.

23.title: 〜を問わず
23.explanation: Says differences in the noun don't matter. Very common in job ads and notices.

examples.jp: 経験の有無を問わず、どなたでも応募できます。
examples.en: Anyone can apply, regardless of experience.

examples.jp: このゲームは年齢を問わず楽しめる。
examples.en: This game can be enjoyed by people of all ages.

23.summary: を問わず means 'regardless of X' — the difference doesn't matter.
23.details:
経験の有無**を問わず**、どなたでも応募できます。
*(Anyone can apply, regardless of experience.)*
このゲームは年齢**を問わず**楽しめる。
*(This game can be enjoyed by people of all ages.)*

Takes nouns that imply a range or a pair: 年齢, 性別, 国籍, 昼夜, 男女, 有無. Very close to にかかわらず; を問わず is especially typical of recruitment ads and rules. 問う literally means 'to ask/question'.

23.title: 〜もかまわず
23.structure: Noun / Verb (Plain) + の + もかまわず
23.explanation: Someone does something without caring about what would normally stop them — often other people's eyes or feelings.

examples.jp: 彼女は人目もかまわず、大声で泣いた。
examples.en: She cried loudly, not caring who saw.

examples.jp: 服が汚れるのもかまわず、子どもたちは泥の中で遊んだ。
examples.en: The children played in the mud without caring that their clothes got dirty.

23.summary: もかまわず describes doing something without caring about what would normally hold you back.
23.details:
彼女は人目**もかまわず**、大声で泣いた。
*(She cried loudly, not caring who saw.)*
服が汚れるの**もかまわず**、子どもたちは泥の中で遊んだ。
*(The children played in the mud without caring that their clothes got dirty.)*

Usually describes someone else's behavior, often with a slightly critical or surprised tone. 人目もかまわず ('without caring who's watching') is the most common phrase. かまう means 'to mind'.

23.title: 〜はさておき
23.explanation: Puts one topic on hold to move to the main point.

examples.jp: 冗談はさておき、本題に入りましょう。
examples.en: Joking aside, let's get down to business.

examples.jp: 細かい点はさておき、全体の方向性を決めよう。
examples.en: Leaving the details aside, let's decide on the overall direction.

23.summary: はさておき puts a topic on hold to get to what matters more.
23.details:
冗談**はさておき**、本題に入りましょう。
*(Joking aside, let's get down to business.)*
細かい点**はさておき**、全体の方向性を決めよう。
*(Leaving the details aside, let's decide on the overall direction.)*

Very common in speech: 冗談はさておき ('joking aside'), それはさておき ('anyway'). Close to はともかく (Lesson 5); はさておき is more about switching topics.

24.title: 〜抜く
24.meaning: Do ~ to the end / Do ~ thoroughly
24.explanation: Doing something completely, to the very end, despite difficulty.

examples.jp: 彼は最後までマラソンを走り抜いた。
examples.en: He ran the marathon all the way to the finish.

examples.jp: 考え抜いた末に、留学することにした。
examples.en: After thinking it through thoroughly, I decided to study abroad.

24.summary: 抜く means doing something all the way through, overcoming difficulty.
24.details:
彼は最後までマラソンを走り**抜いた**。
*(He ran the marathon all the way to the finish.)*
考え**抜いた**末に、留学することにした。
*(After thinking it through thoroughly, I decided to study abroad.)*

Typical combinations: 走り抜く, やり抜く, 考え抜く, 生き抜く, 守り抜く. 困り抜く means 'to be at one's wits' end'. The sense of struggle distinguishes it from 終わる or 切る.

24.title: 〜ことなく
24.explanation: A formal 'without doing', often stressing that something never once happened.

examples.jp: 彼は一日も休むことなく、働き続けた。
examples.en: He kept working without taking a single day off.

examples.jp: あきらめることなく挑戦し続けてください。
examples.en: Please keep trying without giving up.

24.summary: ことなく is a formal 'without (ever) doing X'.
24.details:
彼は一日も休む**ことなく**、働き続けた。
*(He kept working without taking a single day off.)*
あきらめる**ことなく**挑戦し続けてください。
*(Please keep trying without giving up.)*

A written version of ないで／ずに (N3), often with 一度も, 一日も, 決して. It suits formal speeches and writing. ことなしに (N1) is related but means 'without X, Y is impossible'.

24.title: 〜抜きで／〜抜きに
24.structure: Noun + 抜きで・抜きに・抜きの + Noun / Noun + を抜きにして（は）
24.explanation: Something is done without the usual element. を抜きにしては means it is impossible without that element.

examples.jp: 今日は仕事の話は抜きで、楽しく飲みましょう。
examples.en: Let's leave work talk out of it today and enjoy our drinks.

examples.jp: 日本の経済は、自動車産業を抜きにしては語れない。
examples.en: You can't talk about the Japanese economy without the auto industry.

24.summary: 抜きで means 'without X' (leaving it out); を抜きにしては means 'impossible without X'.
24.details:
今日は仕事の話は**抜きで**、楽しく飲みましょう。
*(Let's leave work talk out of it today and enjoy our drinks.)*
日本の経済は、自動車産業を**抜きにしては**語れない。
*(You can't talk about the Japanese economy without the auto industry.)*

In everyday life: 朝ご飯抜き ('skipping breakfast'), わさび抜き ('no wasabi'). With しては the second clause is negative: 〜を抜きにしては語れない／考えられない.

24.title: 〜あまり（に）
24.meaning: So ~ that ~ / Out of too much ~
24.structure: Verb (Dictionary / た-form) / Noun + の + あまり（に）
24.explanation: An emotion or state is so extreme that it causes an unusual or bad result.

examples.jp: 緊張のあまり、何も話せなくなった。
examples.en: I was so nervous that I couldn't say anything.

examples.jp: 子どもを心配するあまり、親はつい口を出してしまう。
examples.en: Parents worry so much about their children that they can't help interfering.

24.summary: あまり（に） means 'because of excessive X' — an extreme feeling causes an unusual result.
24.details:
緊張の**あまり**、何も話せなくなった。
*(I was so nervous that I couldn't say anything.)*
子どもを心配する**あまり**、親はつい口を出してしまう。
*(Parents worry so much about their children that they can't help interfering.)*

Usually with words of emotion: 緊張, 心配, 喜び, 悲しみ, 驚き. This is a different pattern from the N3 adverb あまりにも ('too'), though they share the idea of excess.

25.title: 〜につき
25.explanation: In notices: 'because of'. With numbers: 'per' or 'for each'.

examples.jp: 本日は定休日につき、お休みさせていただきます。
examples.en: We are closed today, as it is our regular holiday.

examples.jp: 参加費は一人につき1,000円です。
examples.en: The participation fee is 1,000 yen per person.

25.summary: につき means 'due to' on formal signs and notices, or 'per' with quantities.
25.details:
本日は定休日**につき**、お休みさせていただきます。
*(We are closed today, as it is our regular holiday.)*
参加費は一人**につき**1,000円です。
*(The participation fee is 1,000 yen per person.)*

The 'due to' use appears almost only on signs and notices: 工事中につき ('under construction'), 準備中につき. In conversation, use ので or ため instead. Different from について (N3, 'about').

25.title: 〜上（じょう）
25.meaning: From the standpoint of ~ / In terms of ~
25.structure: Noun + 上（じょう） / Noun + 上の + Noun
25.explanation: A suffix meaning 'from the point of view of' a field such as law, education or health.

examples.jp: その行為は法律上、問題がある。
examples.en: That act is problematic from a legal standpoint.

examples.jp: 子どもの教育上、よくない番組だ。
examples.en: It's a show that's not good for children's education.

25.summary: 上（じょう） turns a noun into 'from the standpoint of X' — legally, educationally, etc.
25.details:
その行為は法律**上**、問題がある。
*(That act is problematic from a legal standpoint.)*
子どもの教育**上**、よくない番組だ。
*(It's a show that's not good for children's education.)*

Read じょう. Common compounds: 法律上, 教育上, 健康上, 歴史上, 立場上, 仕事上, 表面上 ('on the surface'). Don't confuse it with 〜上で (N3, 'after doing'), or with 上に (N3, 'besides').

25.title: 〜ようでは
25.explanation: Criticizes a current behavior: if it continues, a bad result will follow.

examples.jp: こんな簡単な問題が解けないようでは、合格は無理だ。
examples.en: If you can't solve a simple problem like this, passing is out of the question.

examples.jp: 毎朝遅刻するようでは、信用されない。
examples.en: If you're late every morning, nobody will trust you.

25.summary: ようでは criticizes a behavior: 'if you keep doing X, Y (bad) will happen'.
25.details:
こんな簡単な問題が解けない**ようでは**、合格は無理だ。
*(If you can't solve a simple problem like this, passing is out of the question.)*
毎朝遅刻する**ようでは**、信用されない。
*(If you're late every morning, nobody will trust you.)*

The second clause is negative (無理だ, 困る, だめだ). It's often used for advice or a warning from a superior. The casual form is ようじゃ.

25.title: 〜ようによっては
25.structure: Verb (ます-stem) + ようによっては
25.explanation: The way you look at or do something changes the result.

examples.jp: 考えようによっては、この失敗はいい経験だった。
examples.en: Depending on how you look at it, this failure was a good experience.

examples.jp: この古い服も、使いようによってはまだ役に立つ。
examples.en: Even these old clothes can still be useful, depending on how you use them.

25.summary: ようによっては means 'depending on how you do or see it, the result can change'.
25.details:
考え**ようによっては**、この失敗はいい経験だった。
*(Depending on how you look at it, this failure was a good experience.)*
この古い服も、使い**ようによっては**まだ役に立つ。
*(Even these old clothes can still be useful, depending on how you use them.)*

The most common verbs are 考える, 見る, 言う, 使う, and 考えようによっては is a set phrase for offering a more positive view. よう here means 'way of doing', as in 〜ようがない (N3).

26.title: 〜（よ）うではないか
26.structure: Verb (volitional form) + ではないか・ではありませんか・じゃないか
26.explanation: A strong, formal invitation to a group to act together. Common in speeches.

examples.jp: みんなで力を合わせて、この町を守ろうではないか。
examples.en: Let us join forces and protect this town together.

examples.jp: もう一度話し合ってみようじゃないか。
examples.en: Come on, let's try talking it over once more.

26.summary: （よ）うではないか is a rousing 'let us...' addressed to a group.
26.details:
みんなで力を合わせて、この町を守ろう**ではないか**。
*(Let us join forces and protect this town together.)*
もう一度話し合ってみよう**じゃないか**。
*(Come on, let's try talking it over once more.)*

Typical of speeches, slogans and editorials. In speech, men often use 〜ようじゃないか. It sounds much stronger than 〜ましょう, and it's not used for small personal suggestions.

26.title: 〜やら〜やら
26.meaning: What with ~ and ~ / Things like ~ and ~
26.structure: Noun / Verb (Dictionary) / い-Adj + やら + ... + やら
26.explanation: Lists a few examples, often to show a confused or overwhelming situation.

examples.jp: 引っ越しの準備やら仕事やらで、毎日忙しい。
examples.en: What with preparing to move and work and so on, I'm busy every day.

examples.jp: 合格の知らせを聞いて、うれしいやら驚いたやらで、言葉が出なかった。
examples.en: When I heard I'd passed, I was so happy and surprised I couldn't speak.

26.summary: やら〜やら lists examples of a hectic or mixed-up situation — 'what with X and Y'.
26.details:
引っ越しの準備**やら**仕事やらで、毎日忙しい。
*(What with preparing to move and work and so on, I'm busy every day.)*
合格の知らせを聞いて、うれしい**やら**驚いたやらで、言葉が出なかった。
*(When I heard I'd passed, I was so happy and surprised I couldn't speak.)*

Often describes being overwhelmed or having mixed feelings (うれしいやら恥ずかしいやら). Compared with や〜など (N5) or とか〜とか (N4), it adds a sense of chaos or a jumble of things.

26.title: 〜かというと
26.meaning: If you ask whether ~ (actually, not) / As for why ~
26.structure: Question word / Verb (Plain) + かというと・かといえば
26.explanation: Raises a question and then answers it — often to deny the assumption behind it.

examples.jp: 高い服がいい服かというと、そうとも限らない。
examples.en: If you ask whether expensive clothes are good clothes, that's not necessarily true.

examples.jp: なぜ遅れたかというと、電車が止まったからだ。
examples.en: As for why I was late, it's because the trains stopped.

26.summary: かというと raises a question to answer it — often rejecting the assumption, or explaining a reason.
26.details:
高い服がいい服**かというと**、そうとも限らない。
*(If you ask whether expensive clothes are good clothes, that's not necessarily true.)*
なぜ遅れた**かというと**、電車が止まったからだ。
*(As for why I was late, it's because the trains stopped.)*

Two uses: 'is X really true? not necessarily' (そうとは限らない, そうでもない), and with a question word to set up an explanation (なぜ〜かというと〜からだ). The second use is common in speeches and written explanations.
